Cc: Procurement <procurement@securegrid.com>

Subject: Onboarding: disconnected delivery & signing expectations

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. We're kicking off a private VPC-on-prem onboarding for a SecureGrid EU customer that requires fully disconnected delivery of images and runtime artifacts. Before we schedule the walkthrough we need to validate a few things about Redwood's operator signing and activation model:

- Canonical manifest schema you expect (fields, hash algorithms).
- Operator signing ceremony pattern (two-person activation? HSM-backed vs ephemeral keys).
- Hotfix/urgent patch path for customers with sealed networks.
- Evidence we can pass to our auditors for chain-of-custody (who signs what, timestamps, courier metadata).

Attached is our pre-assessment checklist; procurement also flagged the need for a scoped SOW / DocuSign. Can your team propose a minimal working flow and a rough timeline?

Thanks,
Ian
SecureGrid — Head of Integrations

Attachments: securegrid_pre-assessment_checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Marshall <ian.marshall@securegrid.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T16:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: disconnected delivery & signing expectations

Ian — appreciate the checklist, looks thorough. High level we propose a 3-stage pattern that balances auditability with operator ergonomics:

1) Build & originate
   - Model/artifact build in Redwood build farm. We generate a canonical manifest (JSON) containing artifact SHA256, build metadata, provenance link, and signing policy reference.

2) Transfer & attestation
   - For disconnected delivery we produce a signed-manifest (attached example) and a signed envelope per-transfer. Signatures are HSM-backed on Redwood side; customer may provide an acceptance signature during on-site operator ceremony.

3) Operator activation
   - Two-person operator activation recommended: operator A verifies manifest/hash, operator B performs activation using a locally-held activation token. All steps timestamped and recorded in an audit log artifact shipped with the bundle.

Questions for you (to scope the SOW):
- Do you require Redwood to export our HSM public certificate for external verification, or will you perform independent notarization?
- Are SHA256 hashes sufficient, or do you require SHA512/Ed25519 signatures for future-proofing?
- Expected acceptance window on site (hours) and whether the operator team can perform a remote verification callback during acceptance (we can support an ephemeral, single-use callback channel if permitted).

I'm attaching our internal notes on the disconnected provisioning flow and an example signed-manifest. Monica, can you review operator checklist items for the activation gating?

Best,
Priya
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_offline_provisioning_notes_v1.pdf, signed-manifest-20261112.json (json)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ian Marshall <ian.marshall@securegrid.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T18:40:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: disconnected delivery & signing expectations

Priya / Ian — quick runbook notes from the operator/ops perspective:

- Acceptance criteria (pre-activation): manifest hash matches artifact hash, courier seal id present, operator roster entry present in manifest (names + badge ids).
- Activation gating: successful smoke tests (network isolation, token exchange), signed attestation from two operators (we provide an operator_activation_checklist_v2.pdf).
- Rollback gating: keep a retained snapshot with unsealed images for 72 hours; activation generates an immutable activation record stored both in the shipped audit bundle and our remote retention (if customer opts-in).

Delta/patches: use a content-addressed delta (tree-of-hashes) so operator only receives deltas with their own signed delta-manifests. This reduces courier payload and gives clear traceability.

Timeline (ballpark):
- Week 0: SOW & procurement sign-off
- Week 1: Generate build + signed-manifest, exchange certs
- Week 2: Physical shipment + operator rehearsal
- Week 3: On-site activation window + final audit packet delivered

I'll attach the operator checklist and a short template for courier metadata capture.

-Monica
Manager, Field Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator_activation_checklist_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Ian Marshall <ian.marshall@securegrid.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@securegrid.com>, Ops <ops@securegrid.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding: disconnected delivery & signing expectations

Thanks — that flow is exactly what procurement and our auditors were hoping to see. A couple of notes and confirmations:

- Auditors will want the Redwood HSM public cert and the manifest schema. We will perform an independent notarization step post-delivery (not a blocker).
- SHA256 + Ed25519 signatures are preferred; we can store both in the manifest.
- Two-person activation is required. We will provide operator IDs and will sign the acceptance record on-site.
- For emergency hotfixes we need a sealed emergency channel: Redwood publishes an emergency hotfix manifest to a sealed courier envelope; on-site operators will open under a recorded ceremony with live audit recording.

Procurement also attached the SOW for signature (DocuSign link below). Can we do a technical walkthrough next Wednesday (2026-11-18) at 10:00 CET to go over the manifest fields and the courier metadata capture template?

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/DocuSign/eniq/signon/securegrid-sow-20261112

—Ian
